_why: Tail family for ISCO minor group 962 (Other Elementary Work). Bound at MINOR level (specificity 30) rather than per unit group: the 962x units are narrow industrial specialisations whose workers would get near-identical questions, and 158 near-duplicate packs would be padding that LOOKS like coverage. A unit-level family always wins over this one — that is what the six specificity levels are for.
_v2: REMOVES `tools_owned`. Elementary work is done with equipment the site supplies — jhadu, pocha, bucket, cart — so 'do you own your own' filters nobody and flatters nobody. Kept in the skilled trades next door, where a worker really does arrive with a kit and contractors really do choose on it. Phase 6 (#615) stamped one shared block onto every cluster it could not differentiate; this is the row that block got wrong.
review_note: v2 removes tools_owned (elementary cluster). v1 is deprecated in the same commit — the corpus validator refuses a second ACTIVE pack for one family+locale, because the resolver must never have to choose.
